{{Short description|Species of plant}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2026}} {{Speciesbox |image = Plain tiger (Danaus chrysippus chrysippus) on dwarf poinciana (Caesalpinia pulcherrima f. rosea).jpg |image_caption = ''Caesalpinia pulcherrima'' f. ''rosea''
buds and flowers |status = LC |status_system = IUCN3.1 |status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI) |author2=IUCN SSC Global Tree Specialist Group |date=2019 |title=''Caesalpinia pulcherrima'' |article-number=e.T130102665A148994097 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2019-2.RLTS.T130102665A148994097.en |access-date=16 December 2022}} |genus = Caesalpinia |species = pulcherrima |authority = ([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) [[Olof Swartz|Sw.]] |synonyms = {{Specieslist |Caesalpinia lutea| |Poinciana pulcherrima|L. }} |synonyms_ref = {{GRIN | accessdate = 3 December 2010}} }} '''''Caesalpinia pulcherrima''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[pea]] family [[Fabaceae]], native to the tropics and [[subtropics]] of the Americas. It could be native to Central America,{{cite web |title=Tropical Flower Guide |url=http://tropicalflowerguide.com/dwarf-poinciana-tropical-tree.html |access-date=30 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014095423/http://www.tropicalflowerguide.com/dwarf-poinciana-tropical-tree.html |archive-date=14 October 2012}} but its exact origin is unknown due to widespread cultivation. Common names for this species include '''poinciana''', '''peacock flower''', '''red bird of paradise''', '''Mexican bird of paradise''', '''dwarf poinciana''', '''pride of Barbados''', '''flos pavonis''', and '''''flamboyant-de-jardin'''''.{{citation needed|date=January 2019}} ==Description== [[File:Peacock Flower or Pride-of-Barbados -- Caesalpinia pulcherrima.jpg|thumb|Flowers at various stages of blooming]] It is a [[shrub]] growing to 3 m tall. In climates with few to no frosts, this plant will grow larger and is semievergreen. In Hawaii this plant is evergreen and grows over 5 m tall. Grown in climates with light to moderate freezing, it will die back to the ground during the winter, but will rebound in mid- to late spring. This species is more sensitive to cold than others. The [[leaf|leaves]] are bipinnate, 20–40 cm long, bearing three to 10 pairs of pinnae, each with six to 10 pairs of leaflets 15–25 mm long and 10–15 mm broad. The [[flower]]s are borne in [[raceme]]s up to 20 cm long, each flower with five yellow, orange, or red petals. The fruit is a [[legume|pod]] 6–12 cm long. ==Taxonomy== ''Poinciana pulcherrima'' is a synonym of ''Caesalpinia pulcherrima''.{{cite web |title=Poinciana pulcherrima L. — The Plant List |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/ild-950 |website=www.theplantlist.org |language=en}} == Symbolism == ''Caesalpinia pulcherrima'' is the [[List of national flowers|national flower]] of the Caribbean island of [[Barbados]], and is depicted on the upper left and right corners of the [[Queen's Personal Barbadian Flag|Queen Elizabeth II's personal Barbadian flag]]. ==Uses== ===Food=== All seeds of ''Caesalpinia'' are poisonous. However, the seeds of some species are edible before they reach maturity (e.g. immature seeds of ''C. pulcherrima'') or after treatment (e.g. ''C. bonduc'' after roasting).{{cite book |title=Handbook of Poisonous and Injurious Plants |author1=Lewis Nelson |author2=Richard D. Shih |author3=Michael J. Balick}} ===Traditional medicine=== [[Maria Sibylla Merian]], a 17th-century artist, encountered this plant in the [[Dutch colony]] of [[Surinam (Dutch colony)|Surinam]].{{cite web |last1=Counter |first1=S. Allen |title=Amazing mystery: A medicine man understood the secrets of this plant long before we did. How? |url=https://archive.boston.com/news/education/higher/articles/2006/07/24/amazing_mystery/ |access-date=22 February 2019 |publisher=Boston Globe |date=24 July 2006 |language=en}} In her work, ''Metamorphosis insectorum Surinamensium'', Merian recorded that African slaves and native Indian populations used the ''flos pavonis'' or ''peacock flower'' as an [[abortifacient]] in their practice of [[traditional medicine]].{{cite book |last1=Schiebinger |first1=Londa |title=Plants and empire: colonial bioprospecting in the Atlantic world |date=2007 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge, Massachusetts |isbn=978-0-674-02568-4 |edition=[Nachdr.].}} She wrote:
The Indians, who are not treated well by their Dutch masters, use the seeds [of this plant] to abort their children, so that their children will not become slaves like they are. The black slaves from Guinea and Angola have demanded to be well treated, threatening to refuse to have children. They told me this themselves.{{cite web |last1=Edwards |first1=Stassa |title=The History of Abortifacients |url=https://jezebel.com/the-history-of-abortifacients-1658993381 |website=Jezebel |date=18 November 2014}}
The leaves, flower, bark, and seeds of ''C. pulcherrima'' were also used by [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|American Indians]] in traditional medicine as abortifacients and for suicide by enslaved peoples. ===Ornamental=== ''Caesalpinia pulcherrima'' is the most widely cultivated species in the genus ''Caesalpinia''. It is a striking ornamental plant, widely grown in domestic and public gardens in warm climates with mild winters, and has a beautiful inflorescence in yellow, red, and orange. Its small size and the fact that it tolerates [[pruning]] well allows it to be planted in groups to form a [[hedgerow]]; it can be also used to attract [[hummingbird]]s.Frisch, J.D. & Frisch, C.D., ''Aves Brasileiras e Plantas que as atraem'', São Paulo: Dalgas Ecotec, 2005, 398, {{ISBN|978-85-85015-07-7}} In cultivation in the UK this plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/19624/i-Caesalpinia-pulcherrima-i/Details |title=RHS Plantfinder - ''Caesalpina pulcherrima'' |access-date=12 January 2018}} ==Gallery== File:Peacock flower overview 01.jpg|orange red variant flower File:Pollen grains of Caesalpinia pulcherrima (cropped).jpg|Pollen grains File:Peacock flower blooming.jpg|Buds opening File:Caesalpinia pulcherrima yellow variety in Mihintale, Sri Lanka.jpg|Yellow flowers File:Caesalpinia pulcherrima - Peacock Flower.jpg|"Peacock" flower File:Bunga Merak (Peacock Flower).jpg|Red Peacock Flower ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category-inline}} {{WestAfricanPlants|Caesalpinia pulcherrima}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q1428973}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Caesalpinieae]] [[Category:Flora of Central America]] [[Category:Medicinal plants of Central America]] [[Category:Plants described in 1791]] [[Category:National symbols of Barbados]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Flora without expected TNC conservation status]]
